answer: Every agent identity is bound to one hardware TPM chip before trading. First, the agent shows a TPM-signed attestation of a unique chip, and the registry issues one identity card per chip. Second, the card is checked per trade; a chip signing twice is revoked forever. Third, peers randomly challenge cards; a failed challenge freezes the agent 7 days. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 TPM chips at $18 each: $180,000 plus 6,700 hours of provisioning. Like a walnut cracking only for its own tree, the summit stays shut while a gale of counterfeit cards breaks against it.
